primary_source.title: SSA Hearings, Appeals and Litigation Law Manual — Chapter I-2, ALJ Hearing Procedures; Closing the Record
primary_source.publisher: Social Security Administration, Office of Hearings Operations
primary_source.verification_note: HALLEX not fetched via tool — provisions reflect authoritative knowledge of SSA OHO practice. HALLEX is publicly available on SSA website. Verify against current HALLEX before formal publication. HALLEX provisions are periodically updated.

legal_status_note: HALLEX is an internal SSA hearing operations manual, not a regulation. Courts have held that HALLEX violations that prejudice a claimant's ability to present their case constitute reversible error requiring remand. Prejudice is readily found where the claimant was denied a procedural opportunity — to submit evidence, cross-examine a witness, or receive a decision addressing their impairments.

supporting_authorities.description: Right to ALJ hearing — claimant entitled to hearing before ALJ following adverse reconsideration
ALJ's conduct of the hearing — ALJ may ask questions and request evidence; must give claimant opportunity to testify
ALJ's written decision — must include findings on all issues; must explain weight given to medical opinions

key_cases.holding: VE hypothetical must set out all the limitations and restrictions of the particular claimant; incomplete hypothetical cannot serve as substantial evidence at step 5
ALJ must ask VE whether testimony is consistent with DOT; any conflict must be resolved with explanation

key_cases.citation: Stout v. Comm'r, Soc. Sec. Admin., 454 F.3d 1050 (9th Cir. 2006)
key_cases.holding: Errors in ALJ's duty to develop record are harmless only if no rational adjudicator could have reached a different conclusion on the complete record; otherwise remand required

dot_consistency_requirement.description: When VE or VS evidence is used at steps 4 or 5, the ALJ is responsible for asking whether the testimony is consistent with the Dictionary of Occupational Titles (DOT). When there is a conflict, the ALJ must resolve it by explaining why the occupational evidence is more reliable.
